atoms.canonical_statement: The Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure aims to standardize heart failure terminology and classification for clinicians, researchers, health systems, and policymakers, with the goal of improving prevention, early detection, management, and global cardiovascular health.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The document updates the first Universal Definition of Heart Failure through a joint AHA, ACC, ESC, and WHF task force, in collaboration with HFSA, the HFA of the ESC, and JHFS.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The document explicitly states that it is not a clinical practice guideline or a clinical decision support document; treatment recommendations are reserved for professional society heart failure guidelines.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The consensus reaffirms the stage A through D heart failure staging system from the first Universal Definition while revising phenotype, cause, trajectory, geographic, and mimic terminology.

source_anchor.section: Definition and criteria for stages of HF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The 2026 update groups heart failure phenotypes as reduced ejection fraction, preserved ejection fraction, and improved ejection fraction, proposes a universal classification of causes, and incorporates improvement, remission, recovery, social determinants, and geographic variation into the framework.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Heart failure is defined as a clinical syndrome with diverse causes, characterized by typical symptoms, physical examination signs, and laboratory or imaging abnormalities suggesting pulmonary or systemic congestion or altered cardiac output attributable to an underlying structural or functional cardiac abnormality.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Diagnostic certainty for heart failure increases with elevated BNP or NT-BNP or imaging evidence of pulmonary congestion or elevated intracardiac filling pressures, but the diagnosis depends on the accumulation of suggestive features rather than any single test.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Normal natriuretic peptide levels do not exclude heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, because some affected individuals have unequivocally elevated ventricular filling pressures at rest or with exercise despite normal peptide levels.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Once symptomatic heart failure has been diagnosed, individuals are generally considered to retain the diagnosis permanently even when their clinical condition improves with treatment.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Stage A identifies individuals at risk for heart failure who have no current or prior heart failure symptoms or signs, no structural cardiac changes, and no elevated biomarkers of heart disease.

source_anchor.section: Table 1. Stages in the development and progression of HF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Stage B, termed pre-heart failure, identifies individuals without current or prior heart failure symptoms or signs who have structural cardiac abnormalities, abnormal cardiac function, or elevated natriuretic peptide or cardiac troponin levels.

source_anchor.section: Table 1. Stages in the development and progression of HF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Stage C identifies individuals with current or prior heart failure symptoms or signs caused by a structural or functional cardiac abnormality.

source_anchor.section: Table 1. Stages in the development and progression of HF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Stage D identifies advanced heart failure with severe symptoms or signs at rest or minimal exertion, recurrent hospitalizations despite guideline-directed medical therapy, refractory disease or treatment intolerance, and a need to consider advanced or palliative therapies.

source_anchor.section: Table 1. Stages in the development and progression of HF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The panel retains the term pre-heart failure for stage B to emphasize early detection, close monitoring, and proactive management intended to prevent symptomatic heart failure.

source_anchor.section: Definition and criteria for stages of HF

atoms.canonical_statement: The consensus identifies poverty, lack of education, neighborhood deprivation, and other social disparities as factors associated with incident heart failure and worse prognosis, with multiple social vulnerabilities having cumulative effects.

source_anchor.section: Definition and criteria for stages of HF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The panel gives special attention to cardiometabolic stage A risk factors including overweight, obesity, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes because their prevalence is increasing and preventive treatment opportunities have expanded.

source_anchor.section: Definition and criteria for stages of HF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The document reports that therapies including SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and finerenone in appropriate high-risk populations have reduced the risk of new-onset heart failure; these statements summarize cited evidence rather than constitute treatment recommendations from this consensus document.

source_anchor.section: Definition and criteria for stages of HF

atoms.canonical_statement: The consensus describes a risk gradient from stage A to stage B and states that stage B carries greater short-term risk of progression to overt heart failure, supporting more intensive proactive strategies in pre-heart failure.

source_anchor.section: Definition and criteria for stages of HF

atoms.canonical_statement: Natriuretic peptide screening combined with clinical risk factors may help identify presymptomatic individuals who could benefit from heart failure therapies, and circulating troponin and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio may add information in higher-risk groups.

source_anchor.section: Definition and criteria for stages of HF

atoms.canonical_statement: Artificial intelligence-enabled ECG is presented as a promising screening approach for left ventricular systolic dysfunction and structural heart disease, but the document states that further studies are needed to establish impact across populations, individual outcomes, and implementation feasibility, especially in resource-limited settings.

atoms.canonical_statement: The consensus states that fixed LVEF cutoffs used in prior heart failure classifications are arbitrary and affected by measurement variability, imaging modality, and possible differences by sex, age, and ethnicity.

source_anchor.section: Classification of HF according to LVEF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The document reports an approximate lower limit of normal LVEF of 53% for women and 52% for men, with slightly higher thresholds among people of Asian origin, and states that LVEF below 50% is unlikely to represent normal function regardless of sex, age, or self-reported race and ethnicity.

source_anchor.section: Classification of HF according to LVEF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The Second Universal Definition moves away from universal numeric LVEF cutoffs and uses three clinically actionable groups: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and heart failure with improved ejection fraction.

source_anchor.section: Classification of HF according to LVEF

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The revised LVEF framework allows the clinician to account for sex, age, ethnicity, and individual context, so the exact threshold used to classify reduced ejection fraction need not be identical in every case.

source_anchor.section: Classification of HF according to LVEF

atoms.canonical_statement: The panel emphasizes identifying the specific cause of heart failure because cause can change diagnostic strategy, prognosis, and targeted therapy beyond standard heart failure treatment.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The proposed universal classification of heart failure causes is independent of LVEF and includes ischemic, hypertensive, valvular, arrhythmia-related, infiltrative, infective, inflammatory, toxic, heritable, pericardial, metabolic or nutritional, pregnancy-related, stress-induced, pulmonary or right-sided, congenital, high-output mediated, other, and idiopathic causes.

atoms.canonical_statement: A cited population study of 92 clinically recognized heart failure risk factors is summarized as finding that almost 85% of individuals with heart failure had at least one identifiable pathogenic risk factor amenable to preventive treatment during the five years before diagnosis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The proposed cause list is not exhaustive, categories may overlap, and deep phenotyping or new genetic findings may lead to reclassification, including movement of some idiopathic cardiomyopathies into genetic or familial categories.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The consensus states that the spectrum of cardiovascular disease leading to heart failure differs materially between high-income and low- and middle-income settings and is changing with migration and industrialization.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: A cited worldwide risk-factor synthesis is summarized as attributing ischemic heart disease to more than half of heart failure cases in Western high-income and Eastern and Central European regions, 30% to 40% in several Asian and Latin American regions, and less than 10% in sub-Saharan Africa.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The same geographic synthesis is summarized as identifying hypertension as a common contributor in Eastern and Central Europe and sub-Saharan Africa, while rheumatic heart disease contributed particularly in East Asia and sub-Saharan Africa.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: A cited 195-country analysis is summarized as reporting global 2017 age-standardized heart failure prevalence contributions of 26.5% from ischemic heart disease, 26.2% from hypertensive heart disease, and 23.4% from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, with large regional differences.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The document describes younger heart failure presentation in lower- and middle-income regions and gives examples of region-specific phenotypes, including lean diabetic HFpEF in Southeast Asia, Chagas disease in Latin America, and hypertensive heart disease and peripartum cardiomyopathy in Africa.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The panel identifies a shortage of high-quality data on heart failure prevalence, causes, and outcomes in many low- and middle-income countries and notes the near absence of sub-Saharan African participants in heart failure trials, limiting global generalizability.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Heart failure is framed as a dynamic syndrome whose clinical trajectory changes over time with symptoms, signs, disease progression, improvement, remission, or recovery.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The document describes the conventional improved-ejection-fraction phenotype as prior reduced LVEF followed by an increase of at least 10 percentage points to a new LVEF above 40%, while cautioning that an LVEF-only definition does not capture the full heart failure phenotype.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Improvement is defined as better LVEF despite ongoing structural or clinical abnormalities.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Remission is defined as normalized LVEF with minimal symptoms and stable biomarkers while acknowledging persistent vulnerability to relapse.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Recovery is defined as sustained normalization of cardiac structure, function, biomarkers, and symptoms over extended follow-up and is described as occurring in only a minority of patients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The panel states that LVEF improvement alone does not mean heart failure has resolved and that patients with improved ejection fraction remain at risk for recurrent ventricular dysfunction, supporting continued guideline-directed medical therapy and longitudinal surveillance.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The term stable heart failure is rejected as a misnomer because people with heart failure retain residual risk of worsening symptoms, hospitalization, and sudden cardiac death even when clinically stable.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Worsening heart failure is defined as progressive deterioration in symptoms, signs, and quality of life in a person with a prior heart failure diagnosis; it excludes new-onset heart failure and worsening primarily attributable to unrelated precipitating events such as acute coronary syndrome, infection, or poor treatment adherence.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Worsening heart failure can include increased dyspnea or edema, malignant arrhythmias, reduced exercise capacity, higher pulmonary pressures, worsened ventricular function, and increases in BNP, NT-BNP, or cardiac troponin; an unplanned health care encounter is not required for the diagnosis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Decompensated heart failure is distinguished from worsening heart failure by the need for treatment escalation or rescue therapy; it can occur at any point in the heart failure course and may present gradually or acutely.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Treatment intensification in decompensated heart failure commonly includes increased or combination diuretic therapy and guideline-directed medical therapy, with severe cases potentially requiring device, valvular, mechanical circulatory support, transplant, or palliative strategies; the escalation threshold varies with regional practice and resources.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Common cardiovascular precipitants of acute heart failure include acute myocardial infarction or acute coronary syndrome, hypertensive emergency, arrhythmias, and pulmonary embolism; some acute presentations resolve after timely treatment without progressing to chronic heart failure.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Acute noncardiovascular illnesses including kidney injury, liver failure, and respiratory failure may produce acute heart failure through volume overload and neurohormonal mechanisms, and the heart failure syndrome may resolve when the primary cause is treated.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Chronic heart failure may present subacutely over weeks to months with fatigue, exertional dyspnea, or gradual fluid-related weight gain and may be mistaken for deconditioning or aging, making diagnosis more difficult.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Heart failure mimics are defined as conditions inconsistent with a heart failure diagnosis and not pathophysiologically dependent on neurohumoral activation originating from the myocardium.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Coronary artery disease can be a cause of heart failure, coexist with heart failure, precipitate decompensation, or mimic heart failure through exertional dyspnea; the document describes parallel evaluation for coronary disease and heart failure when both are plausible.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Chronic kidney disease can produce dyspnea, exertional limitation, and peripheral edema from inadequate diuresis or disease progression while also being associated with cardiac structural or functional abnormalities and elevated filling pressures.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Third-trimester pregnancy can produce dyspnea, exertional limitation, and edema; natriuretic peptides and echocardiography can help evaluate a myocardial cause, and the document stresses excluding peripartum cardiomyopathy or unmasked preexisting cardiomyopathy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Obesity and deconditioning can cause dyspnea, exercise intolerance, and edema and complicate heart failure diagnosis because physical examination is less specific and natriuretic peptide levels may be falsely normal even when HFpEF is present; invasive exercise hemodynamics may clarify uncertain cases.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that the 2026 definition is a living framework intended to standardize diagnosis and classification while allowing future adaptation as heart failure phenotypes, causes, diagnostic strategies, and evidence change.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline
